subtitle: VuManChu Cipher A is the most-quoted price-chart overlay in crypto trading. It plots eight markers DIRECTLY on the candles, ranked from rare-but-strong (yellow X) to common-but-weak (bull candle). Understanding which marker means what is the difference between informed and astrology.

blocks.content:
The VuManChu indicator suite has two components: Cipher A (this lesson) draws signals ON the price chart; Cipher B (next lesson) draws a separate oscillator pane below. Both are derived from WaveTrend (LazyBear's oscillator) plus an 8-EMA ribbon and a few cross-derived conditions.

This lesson covers Cipher A's eight signal markers — what each one means, how rare each is, and what action (if any) they suggest.

Cipher A starts with an EMA ribbon of 8 lengths: 5, 11, 15, 18, 21, 24, 28, 34. Plotted together they form a smooth, gradient-coloured band.

  • When the ribbon is stacked bullish (EMA-5 highest, EMA-34 lowest), the trend is up. Coloured green / shades of blue.
  • When stacked bearish (EMA-34 highest), the trend is down. Coloured red.
  • When crossing, the trend is transitioning.

The ribbon itself isn't a signal — it's the BACKDROP that contextualises the markers below.

blocks.title: Yellow X is the prize
blocks.content: If you see ONE setup per week worth describing as "textbook", it's a Yellow X. It requires simultaneous conditions: WaveTrend at deep oversold (-60 to -80 zone), RSI between 15-30 (extreme oversold), AND money flow negative. When all align, the bounce probability historically lands in the 75-85% range. Treat Yellow X with the respect that rarity deserves — full size, not half.

A Blood Diamond fires when TWO bearish conditions converge in the same bar: the WaveTrend oscillator crosses down AND the fast EMA crosses below the slow EMA. Think of it as 'the indicator agrees with the ribbon — momentum is officially exhausted.'

Real example from our trading: on 2026-05-27 16:00 UTC, HYPEUSDT printed Blood Diamond + Red Cross + Red Diamond on the same 4H bar. Price was $60.16 with WaveTrend at +60 (overbought). Over the next 16 hours, HYPE dropped from $60 → $57.5 (−4.4%). That marker was the warning.

A Red Diamond by itself fires often — every time the WaveTrend crosses down, regardless of zone. In a strong uptrend, you might see 3-4 per week, most of them meaningless (price just cools off briefly then continues). The Red Diamond becomes meaningful only when paired with other signals:

  • Red Diamond + Red Cross = Blood Diamond (strong)
  • Red Diamond at WaveTrend > +60 = at OB extreme, fade-worthy
  • Red Diamond + RSI > 70 = exhaustion fading from overbought

blocks.title: Don't trade on a single marker
blocks.content: None of the eight markers — even Yellow X — should be a standalone entry trigger. Always confirm with at least one other source: macro context (the MTF EMA verdict from lesson 22.5), the oscillator pane (Cipher B, next lesson), or structural confluence (S/R, FVG). A single marker without confluence has roughly 50% accuracy. Two confluent signals push that to 65%. Three push it to 75%+.
How to use Cipher A practically

The workflow:

  1. Macro filter first: Check the MTF EMA verdict. If "trend_up_confirmed", favor longs. If "trend_down_confirmed", favor shorts. If "reversal_warning" or chop, be cautious about counter-trend.
  2. Mark Cipher A signals over the last 10 bars on your decision timeframe (usually 4H for swings, 1H for scalps).
  3. Score the confluence: ribbon direction + most recent strong marker + macro alignment.
  4. Plan the trade: entry near the marker bar's close, SL beyond the structural anchor, TPs at the next 2-3 levels.

blocks.title: Bottom line
blocks.content: Cipher A's 8 markers form a hierarchy from very rare/strong (Yellow X, Blood Diamond) to common/weak (Bull Candle, Red Diamond alone). Never treat any single marker as a standalone signal — always combine with macro filter + structural confluence. The Yellow X is the trade of the month; everything else is graded weight in a confluence stack.
